conflicts.subject: model
conflicts.detail: Authorization models differ (A: none: every route is open; B: none)
solutions: Choose one authorization model and express the others' rules in it
conflicts.recommended: One authorization model with one permission check function

resolution.decision: Neither app has any authorization (all routes open). Unified app: per-user ownership; one can(user, action, record) check used by every route and query; a user can only read or change their own books, ratings and lists. One role 'reader'; no admin role in v1.

conflicts.subject: rating-scale
conflicts.detail: Shelfie's README and openapi.yaml say ratings are 1-10 in a field named 'score'; Shelfie's code (handler and DB CHECK) and Readr's code both use 1-5 in a field named 'stars'. Building from the docs would make every existing rating mean something different.
solutions: Follow the code: 1-5 integer 'stars' (both apps agree)
Follow Shelfie's docs: 1-10 'score' and rescale any imported data
Store 1-10 internally and show 5 stars
conflicts.recommended: Follow the code: integer 'stars' 1-5, enforced in the API and by a DB CHECK; correct the docs in the new app

resolution.decision: Follow the code, not Shelfie's stale docs: integer 'stars' 1-5, checked in the API (reject non-integers and booleans) and by a DB CHECK. The documented 1-10 'score' is not built.

conflicts.subject: session
conflicts.detail: Session mechanisms differ (A: none (shelfie_session_secret is required at startup but unused); B: none)
solutions: Choose one session mechanism (http-only cookie sessions are the safer default for web apps)
Use tokens only where a client cannot hold cookies
conflicts.recommended: One session mechanism for the whole app

resolution.decision: Neither app has sessions (Shelfie reads a secret it never uses). Unified app: email + password accounts, password hashed with a slow KDF, server-side session row referenced by an http-only, SameSite=Lax, Secure (in production) cookie signed with SESSION_SECRET.

conflicts.subject: export-format
conflicts.detail: Shelfie's README and spec promise CSV at GET /api/v1/books/export.csv; the code serves JSON at GET /api/books/export. The CSV export was never built.
solutions: Build JSON export as the code does
Build CSV as the docs say
Offer both
conflicts.recommended: JSON export as the code does (user: trust what the apps do); CSV recorded as an open question, not built

resolution.decision: JSON export as the code does; CSV (documented only, never built) is not built; left as an open question for the user.

conflicts.subject: documented-services-and-database
conflicts.detail: Shelfie's docs describe three services (catalog, ratings, gateway) each with its own database, on PostgreSQL; the code is one process with one SQLite file and no gateway.
solutions: Design from the code: one process, one database
Design from the docs: three services with a gateway
conflicts.recommended: Ignore the stale service and PostgreSQL claims; choose the architecture on this project's drivers in phase 5

resolution.decision: Stale three-service / PostgreSQL docs are ignored; architecture chosen on this project's drivers in phase 5.

conflicts.subject: list-entries-and-foreign-keys
conflicts.detail: Readr allows the same book on a list twice and never checks that the list or book exist (SQLite foreign keys are off by default).
solutions: Unique (list_id, book_id), foreign keys on, ownership checks
Allow duplicates
conflicts.recommended: Primary key (list_id, book_id), PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON, cascade deletes, ownership checked on list and book

resolution.decision: ReadingListItem primary key (list_id, book_id); PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON; ON DELETE CASCADE from list and book; ownership checked on both.

conflicts.subject: rating-cardinality-and-durability
conflicts.detail: Both apps append a new ratings row on every rating (no key, no uniqueness) and neither ever commits, so ratings pile up and are lost on exit; Shelfie's export repeats a book once per rating.
solutions: One rating per user per book, upsert, commit every write
Keep append-only history
conflicts.recommended: Rating has a unique (user_id, book_id); PUT upserts; every write commits; export shows the current rating

resolution.decision: Rating unique (user_id, book_id); PUT upserts, DELETE clears; every write commits in a transaction; export shows the current rating.

conflicts.subject: book
conflicts.detail: Book exists in A:Book, B:Book; fields not shared: author (only A)
solutions: Merge into one table holding the fields kept features need
Keep separate tables if the two only share a name, and rename one
conflicts.recommended: Merge into one entity; list every field's origin in architecture.json

resolution.decision: One Book entity merged from A:Book and B:Book: id, owner_id (new), title, author (from A, nullable), timestamps.

conflicts.subject: path-prefix
conflicts.detail: Spec uses /api/v1/...; code uses /api/... with no version. Neither app has clients we know of.
solutions: New app uses /api/v1 for every endpoint
Keep unversioned /api
conflicts.recommended: New app uses /api/v1 for every endpoint (one versioning scheme); there is no observed client of the old paths to keep compatible

resolution.decision: Every endpoint under /api/v1; no compatibility shims for Shelfie's unversioned /api paths (no known clients).

conflicts.subject: undocumented-session-secret
conflicts.detail: Shelfie requires SHELFIE_SESSION_SECRET at startup but never uses it, and no doc mentions it.
solutions: Give the new app a documented session secret it actually uses
Drop the variable
conflicts.recommended: One documented SESSION_SECRET in the config module and .env.example (name only), used to sign session cookies

resolution.decision: Replaced by SESSION_SECRET, read in the config module, listed (name only) in .env.example, used to sign session cookies; startup fails with a clear message if unset outside development.
